title: JavaScript and TypeScript Comment Remover
description: Remove parsed comments from JavaScript or TypeScript while preserving string literals, token boundaries, and line numbers.
intro: JavaScript and TypeScript Comment Remover parses source before locating comment ranges. It replaces comment characters with whitespace while preserving line breaks, string literals, and token separation. Unsupported languages and malformed syntax are reported as errors instead of being rewritten by a broad search-and-replace.
audience: JavaScript and TypeScript developers preparing source excerpts for review
input: Valid JavaScript or TypeScript source containing inline or block comments, with the matching language selected in the editor.
outcome: Source text with parsed comment ranges replaced by whitespace, retaining line numbers, string contents, and token boundaries.
review: Check the cleaned source in your own compiler or test suite. Preserve license notices and tool directives when they are needed outside this cleaning task.
bestFor: Small JavaScript and TypeScript excerpts used for documentation or comparison when source comments need to be removed deliberately.
steps: Select JavaScript or TypeScript to match the source syntax.
Paste a snippet or load a supported text file into the editor.
Choose Remove Comments and inspect the cleaned output beside the original.
Save a copy and run project checks before replacing source files.
useCases: Preparing a JavaScript example without explanatory comments.
Removing a TypeScript block comment while retaining type syntax.
Comparing source snippets without comment wording differences.
Keeping source line numbers stable during a documentation cleanup.
commonMistakes: Removing license comments or directives without reviewing their purpose.
Expecting whitespace minimization from a comment-removal operation.
tips: URLs and comment-like text inside string literals remain literal data.
Whitespace is retained where comments separate adjacent tokens.
Keep a copy of the original file before editing a repository.
Use a minifier separately when compact output is the actual goal.

faq.question: Which source languages are supported?
faq.answer: Comment removal currently parses JavaScript and TypeScript. Other language syntax is rejected instead of being edited heuristically.

faq.question: Are strings containing comment markers changed?
faq.answer: No. Parsed string literals, regular expression literals, and template text retain their original content.

faq.question: Why are blank spaces left behind?
faq.answer: Spaces keep token boundaries and line breaks stable after comment text is removed. This tool is not a whitespace minifier.

faq.question: What happens when parsing fails?
faq.answer: An error is displayed and the input is retained. No partially rewritten output is presented as a successful result.

faq.question: Should all comments be removed from project files?
faq.answer: That depends on the project. Review licensing, documentation, and build-tool directives before replacing the original source.

examples.title: URL literal and a trailing comment
examples.description: Language: JavaScript. The URL stays intact and the trailing comment becomes spaces.

examples.title: TypeScript block comment
examples.description: Language: TypeScript. The type annotation and the quoted comment markers remain unchanged.
examples.input:
const label: string = "/* literal */"; /* remove */
export { label };
examples.output:
const label: string = "/* literal */";             
export { label };
